questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: good university, cultural city with a big difference to the culture I am used to

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: it was available, but a bit chaotic, not in a good hierarchy where the most important info wasnt that clear.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: mostly the general info for international students, but the most important info didnt come digital as well, so upon arrival the info wasnt that good.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: pretty easy, but I did it trough a friend

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: that you might end up with a longer commute, and there is a social aspect to living on campus, but I think you get more ownership to the city by living off campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: the course registration process was complicated and confusing, and you dont get a lot of help.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: there are different time slots to first pre-register, then add courses to a course cart, and then to actually registrate, and its all in korean local time, and its difficult to know witch courses you can actually apply for.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: you can email them, but they mostly send out long, general, info manuals where its difficult to know where the correct info is.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: in the end I did succeed, but it was a lot back and forward after I came there. And I wanted some other courses, but it was so unclear witch ones I could take.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Start early, have communcation with your home university in what their restrictions are for courses, and then research the ones available for you. But if its both graduate, and in english, there isnt that much available.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: the professors I had were amazing.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: there were some cool BA courses I wanted to take, and that would be more relevant for my academic theme, but I could only take courses at MA level

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: a bit more strict, but also very rewarding

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
18th centrury british literature
seminar in philosophy of art 
public administration and policy

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: 18th centrury british literature because the professor is extremely talented and enlightened.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: grocerys at the food store is very expensive, also fruit and vegetables are extremely expensive, so I didnt really eat much of that while I was there.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A LOT. so many sports, parties, activities, clubs.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: sports, because you get to know more locals in a not exhange-program. The buddy-program is also good, but its created for the exhange students. the sports is more lowkey and a natural setting. And a lot of fun, different sports you can join.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel around. To Busan or Jeju Island, or just other small cities. Seoul can feel pretty intense.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Not very easy, but as long as you try and work for it, it is very possible to get many local friends.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Dont be to critical to getting other international friends, but make an effort to approach and invite locals.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Maybe the gender roles.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food, and how social their eating out can be.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
-The language feels very different, but a little effort comes a long way. Learning 15 phrases gets you longer than not learning anything. And it is very fun and apprrecciated to know a little bit korean. You get more use of the few things you learn than you would think, even with bad pronunciation. 
-if you want to join sports and so on, it is nice to not live an hour from campus. 
-try to pick courses that are close together timewise, the lectures are often not longer than 3 houres, and it is nice to have long weekends to travel, and not miss any of your classes.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: even though the course registration is stressfull, you can actually go to seoul before everything is fugured out, and then finish the process while you are there. it is possible to change for a long time even in september.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: getting to know such a different city and their culture and history, their history is very interesting and different.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: the balance of being in a very international enviroment, and still getting to know the locals, and not feeling bad about not getting involved enough.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
